_Requested by **Jeremy** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01LbyjhUBfbvjN8y2Mh7apyX?thread=cmsg_01LbyjhUBfbvjN8y2Mh7apyXN9dbp98yfZT4zY8G6i63EV)_

## What this is

The Stellar Map draws your memory as a star system. It only appears in the Nova theme. Open **Memory** and press **Map** at the top right. The map is rebuilt from the files in your Nova folder every time, and nothing is stored separately.

- **What each body is:**
  - Nova is the bright core.
  - You are the ringed planet, from USER.md.
  - People are planets, and topics are gas giants.
  - Goals are stars, and memories are moons.
  - Recent days are comets. Old notes that name no one are asteroids at the edge.
  - A group such as Family is a coloured nebula.
- **Getting around:**
  - Drag, scroll or pinch to move between three scales: Galaxy, System and Orbit.
  - Hovering over a body lights up its threads.
  - Clicking a body opens the inspector, which shows its source file, why it's there, its threads and its moons.
  - From a moon you can **Edit** or **Forget**, with the same Undo the list has.
  - ⌘K searches and flies there. The arrow keys step along threads.
- **Motion:** when the map is idle it moves very slowly, and it pauses while you interact. With reduced motion turned on, it stops moving and flights are instant.

The plain-words review note is in [`docs/stellar-map-review.md`](docs/stellar-map-review.md). It covers what to try and the decisions for you.

## Decisions for you

1. **People, groups, topics and goals now have files.** They follow the way Muse lays things out: `memory/people/`, `memory/groups/`, `memory/topics/` and `workspace/goals/<goal>/GOAL.md`. Nova's system prompt now asks it to keep these files, and `write_file` can write them. Until those files exist, your real map will mostly be your planet and its moons.
2. **The switch is List | Map, not Files | Map | Split.** The Files explorer isn't built yet.
3. **Three things are left out on purpose:**
   - the optional timeline scrubber
   - confirm/remove for inferred threads, because Nova doesn't infer any threads yet
   - depth of field

## Screenshots (the people are made up, because the repo is public)

| Galaxy | Selected |
| --- | --- |
| ![galaxy](https://github.com/jeremyspofford/nova/blob/claude/project-thread-o5r6kx/docs/screenshots/nova-map-galaxy.png?raw=true) | ![selected](https://github.com/jeremyspofford/nova/blob/claude/project-thread-o5r6kx/docs/screenshots/nova-map-selected.png?raw=true) |
| **Orbit** | **A gas giant via ⌘K** |
| ![orbit](https://github.com/jeremyspofford/nova/blob/claude/project-thread-o5r6kx/docs/screenshots/nova-map-orbit.png?raw=true) | ![search](https://github.com/jeremyspofford/nova/blob/claude/project-thread-o5r6kx/docs/screenshots/nova-map-search.png?raw=true) |

`docs/screenshots/` has more: hover, system, moon, reduced motion, empty home and phone.

## Checks

- **`npm run check` passes.** All 137 tests pass. That includes the new `tests/map.test.js`, which covers:
  - the map is rebuilt from the files, and deleting a file removes its body
  - name matching and salience
  - stacking bodies when there are more than about 300
  - an empty home
  - no overlapping bodies

  The token lint and the theme contract also pass.
- **`npm run shots:map` passes 27 of 27 checks in Chromium.** It covers every interaction above, plus Paper (no map), reduced motion, a phone screen and an empty home.
- **Not measured: real frame rates.** The build container has no GPU, so WebGL runs on a software renderer at about 3.5 s per frame. Please try dragging the map on the mini-pc. If it feels slow, the next step is a cheaper planet shader at Galaxy scale.
